subject: Biology
title: Climate Change and Ecosystems
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Climate Change and Ecosystems.

hook.text: Earth's average temperature has risen about 1.1°C since the Industrial Revolution.

buildup.text: Species are shifting ranges toward poles and higher altitudes to find suitable temperatures.

discovery.text: Coral bleaching occurs when warming waters stress corals, expelling the algae they depend on.

twist.text: Some species can't move fast enough. Arctic specialists like polar bears are running out of ice.

climax.text: Climate change doesn't just raise temperatures—it shifts rainfall, seasons, and ocean chemistry.

punchline.text: A warming world reshuffles all of nature.

quiz.question: What causes coral bleaching?
options: Warming waters stress corals and expel their algae

details.summary: Climate change is reshaping ecosystems worldwide by altering temperature, precipitation, and seasonal patterns. Species must adapt, migrate, or face extinction as habitats shift faster than many organisms can respond, disrupting ecological relationships built over millennia.
details.whyItMatters: Climate change threatens ecosystem services that sustain human civilization, from crop pollination to fisheries. Coral reefs, polar ecosystems, and mountain habitats are already showing severe impacts that cascade through food webs.
takeaways: Species are shifting ranges toward poles and higher elevations
Phenological mismatches disconnect species from their food sources
Ocean warming and acidification threaten marine ecosystems globally

faq.question: How does climate change cause phenological mismatches?
faq.answer: When temperatures rise, some species shift their seasonal timing faster than others. Birds may migrate earlier but find that insect prey have not yet emerged, or flowers bloom before their pollinators arrive. These timing mismatches break ecological partnerships.

faq.question: Which ecosystems are most vulnerable to climate change?
faq.answer: Coral reefs are extremely sensitive to temperature increases. Arctic and alpine ecosystems face habitat loss as ice and snow disappear. Tropical cloud forests, mangroves, and coastal wetlands are also highly vulnerable to warming and sea level rise.
